newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African state job cuts save one bln rand a year.
newsitem.headline: S.African state job cuts save one bln rand a year.

text.p: The South African government's public service reduction programme has already saved about one billion rand a year, Public Service Department director general Paseka Ncholo said on Tuesday.
Interviewed during an Intergovernmental Forum meeting in Somerset West, Ncholo said the government had approved 39,800 of about 58,000 applications for a voluntary severance package.
He said 24,124 people had left the government service by the end of last year in terms of the retrenchment deal and the rest would leave by early next year.

"If you add the funded vacancies that we had to abolish, which is about 19,000, that gives you about 60,000 jobs gone out of a total staff complement of around 1.2 million and a saving of about a billion rand a year," he told Reuters.
Ncholo said the offer remained open and applications were still coming in, but the package could come up for review in the next round of public service wage talks due to start on March 10.
Ncholo said the average income of the people seeking retrenchment was higher than the assumed average of 50,000 rand a year and the government was becoming concerned about the loss of skills.
He said about 5,000 applications had been denied as the government increasingly tested applications against the public interest.

"Most of the applications rejected have been handled quite recently. It is happening more because if, for example, you have five computer network managers it is easy to tell the first one he can go, but its more difficult to let the last one go," he sid.
Ncholo said the aim of the restructuring programme was to keep the state's salary bill constant at around 58 percent of non-debt state expenditure for the next three years.

He said the government had planned to sacrifice about 100,000 jobs at an average of 50,000 rand a year, but it might already have achieved the desired saving with the abolition of about 60,000 higher level jobs.
More than 10,000 applications had still to be considered.
